phase3_findings.description: docs/external/rule-sets.md line 69 gives the validation-error path as rule_sets.0.tables.1.columns, but _record_path in src/sqllens/rule_sets.py lines 268-275 renders list positions in brackets, so the emitted text is rule_sets[0].tables[1].columns. Capped at Important by the behavior-inert prose rule because it is a published external page.
src/sqllens/cli.py line 167 separates _unconfirmed_rule_sets from the preceding definition with one blank line instead of two; ruff's default selection does not flag it.

docs/external/rule-sets.md line 99 says sqllens serve prints a warning for an unconfirmed set; serve emits it through the sqllens.rule_sets logger, so visibility depends on the configured log level, while validate really prints to the console.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py lines 433-441: _logged_by_guard treats any non-UnsafeSqlError/RlsError cause as already logged, so an RLS parse failure raised from a ParseError is redacted to the generic kind and logged nowhere, unlike every other guard's fail-closed path.

src/sqllens/agent/factory.py lines 76-84: _RuleSetUserResolver falls back to the shared built-in user with no log record when no rule-set selection is published, while every other rule-set component treats a missing selection as an error.

src/sqllens/config.py lines 752-774: RuleSetsConfig can represent a configured-but-unloaded rule-set file, and every downstream gate keys off the loaded value, so an instance built outside Config validation silently disables the guards.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py lines 234-248: CatalogConfirmation creates an asyncio.Lock at config-load time outside any running loop, and ensure_catalog_confirmed enters it outside the try that converts failures into a structured refusal.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py lines 467-472: RefusalRedactingRunner rebuilds the refusal with type(exc).__new__ plus Exception.__init__, bypassing the type's own constructor; safe only because the one stateful subclass is re-raised earlier.

docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md lines 185 and 191 state the runner call order without the two new runners, as do docs/internal/agent/factory.md line 87 and docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md line 209, while a sibling line in the same file was scoped by this change.

docs/external/rule-sets.md line 125 says every identifier is a decimal string so 5 and "5" are written the same way; that holds for a request value but not for the file, where a bare number fails StrictStr validation.
tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py line 8 describes the example set as listing a predicate column, but the module's shared example mapping carries none; individual tests supply one.
docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md line 3 records a freshness marker two commits behind the branch head, which is itself this branch's documentation commit.
docs/external/configuration.md line 234 still frames row-rule blocks as unlike other sections in rejecting unknown keys; the new rule-sets section rejects them too.
The AGENTS.md architecture tree gains no entry for src/sqllens/rule_sets.py or src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py, although it lists the safety package file by file.
src/sqllens/preflight.py lines 168-174 convert any non-mismatch catalog-check failure into a structured preflight error, and no test covers that branch.

src/sqllens/cli.py lines 105-118 decide whether verify-memory adds its rule-set message when the config fails to load; the environment-variable short-circuit and the unreadable-file fallback are untested.

Nothing drives the agent's SQL tool end to end to check that a rule-set refusal reaches the model carrying the prefix the new prompt rule keys on (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py line 59); the existing test only compares the prompt with the constant.
No regression test asserts that list_data_sources still answers a call with no request metadata while a rule-set file is configured, nor that the bundle manifest gains no rule-set entry.
